quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be alert when children on bikes ride on the sidewalk—they may suddenly move into the road.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is correct?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no traffic is coming.
Use your mirrors and check your blind spot over your left shoulder when passing left.
Return to your lane only when you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Return to your original lane only after you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Is it illegal to drive next to a motorcycle in the same lane?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there seems to be enough space. Motorcycles need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: How should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look at the right side of the road. Do not look at the bright headlights—the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter/skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back to the right lane after passing?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space to return safely to your lane. Make sure there is room between you and the car you passed. When both headlights appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to maneuver as cars.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks need more room to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: When traffic moves at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than most vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few mph slower than most vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles drive much faster or slower than others.

questions.question: Should you ever drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in the lane for a green arrow, you can proceed in the direction of the arrow when the road is clear. This applies whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is coming toward you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
Never.

questions.explanation: You can never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, slow down gently using the brakes. When you are at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force your vehicle back.

questions.question: Your tire blows out. What should you do?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, slow down gradually by removing your foot from the gas. Do not brake hard until your vehicle has slowed down considerably.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge.

questions.question: Your tire blows out. What should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes immediately.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, remove your foot from the gas and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if vehicles are blocking it. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block other traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: When may you turn right on red?

options.text: If there is no sign prohibiting it.
Before pedestrians have crossed the crosswalks.
Before coming to a complete stop.
After a complete stop and only if it is safe and there are no pedestrians or vehicles in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a complete stop and only if it is safe and there are no pedestrians or vehicles in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you may turn right after coming to a complete stop if there is no sign prohibiting it and if it is safe. Always check for pedestrians and other vehicles before turning.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to help prevent crashes. Do not use it to tell a driver or bicyclist to go faster or to get out of your way.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only move when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, check for a gap in traffic, match the speed of traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to be completely clear before merging.

questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch for other traffic and do not assume drivers will clear the lane for you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp in the wrong direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.
